source: MAFF Department of Agricultural Extension (នាយកដ្ឋានផ្សព្វផ្សាយកសិកម្ម), "បច្ចេកទេសដាំដុះសណ្តែកបាយ" (Mung Bean Cultivation Techniques handbook), Kingdom of Cambodia, MAFF, published by the Department of Agricultural Extension. Reference list on the closing page cites additional 2003-dated MAFF/agricultural-extension source booklets on mung bean varieties, seed production, and pest management, plus several international references (Plant Resources of South-East Asia Vol. I, 1992; Talekar & Skinner, Field Guide to Insect Pests of Tropical Asia, 1995; Nelson, Insect Pests of Vegetables, Philippines, 1969; Mung Bean Adaptation Trial, Kbalkoh Station 1996-2000, CLV Network; and a 1991 Bangkok workshop proceedings on Yellow Mosaic Virus). No elibrary.maff.gov.kh URL is visible on the scanned pages provided, so none is given here. Uploaded as a 38-page scanned PDF; no embedded text layer, all content read visually from page images. This is Source C for crop/mung_bean in this knowledge base (Sources A-B were processed in Batch 42).
text: World situation: mung bean is grown in tropical and subtropical regions, especially in Asia, and is described as a leading legume crop of its category. Per a cited 1986 statistic, the crop was reported grown in roughly 60 countries; mung bean is said to occupy about two-thirds of total area planted to comparable pulse crops in that reference, with reported productivity in the range of roughly 470-800 kg/ha. Cambodia situation: within Cambodia the source describes mung bean as suited to flood-recession and residual-moisture land, historically associated with areas such as Battambang and expanding along the Mekong and into Kampong Cham, Kampong Chhnang, Kandal, Prey Veng, Kampot and other provinces, typically on sandy soils along riverbanks and lake shores. A national area/yield/productivity table for 2015-2017 is given: 2015 - cultivated area 53,962 ha, total yield 59,220 tons, productivity 1.10 t/ha; 2016 - cultivated area 49,408 ha (table) / 49,404 ha (accompanying bar chart), total yield 64,137 tons, productivity 1.30 t/ha; 2017 - cultivated area 48,340 ha (table) / 45,340 ha (accompanying bar chart), total yield 53,597 tons, productivity 1.18 t/ha.
caveat: Numeric discrepancy reported, not reconciled: the source's own printed table (page 7) and its accompanying bar chart (page 8) give different cultivated-area figures for 2016 (49,408 vs 49,404 ha) and especially for 2017 (48,340 vs 45,340 ha). Both figures are reported here as printed rather than picking one as correct, per this knowledge base's standing convention.
